A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Mixture-UCB research. Their main text, algorithms, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite retitling and substantial reformatting.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix C report original image- and text-generation experiments, quantitative algorithm comparisons, and sparse-mixture analyses.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix 8.4 retain original empirical comparisons and report additional KID table entries.

M1.justification: CAB, OGD, and the sparse Algorithm 3 retain their procedures. Section 8.3 adds an optional target-sparsity adaptation: start lambda at zero, increase it until the desired number of subscribed arms remains, then stop eliminating arms. This procedure is not specified in v1.

E1.justification: Both evaluate FFHQ, LSUN-Bedroom, AFHQ Cat, CIFAR-10, OpenLLMText, and the same dog, car-style, sofa, and red-bird scenarios. The new introductory FFHQ figure uses retained coverage; the text-generation experiment remains in v2's appendix.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Mixture Oracle, One-Arm Oracle, Vanilla-UCB, and Successive Halving alongside CAB and OGD. The individual generators compared in Tables 1 and 2 also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: V1 Appendix C.4 reports quality-metric weights lambda = 0.2 and 0.5, whereas v2 Section 8.4.3 reports only 0.2. This revises the stated setting; the retained plots do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The sparse one-, two-, and three-arm comparison and the analysis of adding Precision/Density to exclude the CIFAR-10 generator retain their questions, displays, and findings. No new ablation, robustness test, or error analysis is introduced.

E5.justification: V2 supplies standard deviations for the retained KID experiments in Tables 1 and 2, beyond v1's average KID curves. Both specify ten repetitions with different random seeds, so this expands uncertainty reporting without establishing additional runs.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 2 add KID entries while retaining their other scores. The sofa prose changes RKE values from 12.12/14.51 to 7.21/7.57, although the retained illustration still shows the earlier values. New Figure 1 redisplays existing FID results and reports mixture KID uncertainty of 0.07 versus 0.007 in Table 1. These reporting changes do not establish improved performance between versions.

T1.justification: Section 8.3 adds a formal finite-horizon subscription-cost objective, Equation 16, and its desired sparsity-penalized asymptotic target. V1 Appendix B provided the sparse algorithm without this formulation. The concentration and regret theorems and their proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Both claim that mixtures can improve quality/diversity scores, propose quadratic Mixture-UCB optimization, and establish CAB convergence with image/text experiments. V2 foregrounds FID/KID improvements already supported in v1 Appendix C.2; the sparse contribution also remains despite the condensed contribution list.

C2.justification: V2 drops v1's expectation that differently trained text-to-image models should gain more diversity from mixing than same-dataset unconditional models. Its conclusion replaces domain-extension suggestions with the unresolved characterization of when mixtures improve scores. The quality/diversity trade-off and missing OGD regret bound were already discussed in v1.

D1.justification: Section 8.4.2 newly specifies that the online truncated-FFHQ experiment uses a fresh generated-image set; v1 Appendix C.3 did not disclose this distinction. Most encoders, sampling budgets, bandwidths, and code/data access information are retained.

R1.justification: Related work adds Wang et al.'s distributed evaluation and several novelty-evaluation references, including Han et al. and Jiralerspong et al. It removes the comparison with Hu et al.'s prompt-based contextual model-selection work. The central positioning against single-arm and informational bandits remains.

P1.justification: V2 substantially rewrites the abstract and introductory narrative, adds Section 1.1, changes the title, condenses the experimental discussion, and revises the conclusion. It also moves the main-text discussion of text generators into the appendix and reorganizes Appendices A-C under Section 8.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a conference layout, adds the FFHQ montage in Figure 1, and expands both tables with KID columns. Numerous retained figures move between the main text and appendix, including v1 Figures 2, 4, and 5 becoming v2 Figures 11, 7, and 10. Most underlying plots and sample panels remain.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves clarity and completeness through the sparse method's explicit cost formulation, KID results with uncertainty, and clearer empirical motivation. The central theory and experimental coverage remain stable. These benefits are tempered by inconsistent sofa scores, the Figure 1/Table 1 KID uncertainty discrepancy, and the unexplained quality-weight revision, limiting the overall gain.
